🔰Did the BRICS summit in New Delhi bring about real political and financial progress?

👤 Paulo Nogueira Batista Junior, Brazilian economist, former vice president of the BRICS New Development Bank and former executive director of the International Monetary Fund, has assessed the political-diplomatic and financial outcomes of the recent BRICS summit in India in an analysis:

🔹The summit was deemed successful on three political fronts: the near-complete attendance of leaders, the issuance of a comprehensive joint statement despite the group's internal heterogeneity, and the confirmation of signs of rapprochement between China and India, which holds strategic importance for BRICS and the Global South.

🔸On the financial front, the New Development Bank remains the group's most significant practical achievement, yet it has remained limited in terms of membership and is still largely dollarized. The Contingent Reserve Arrangement has yet to become operational, and progress on BRICS Pay remains in its early stages.

🔹Internal obstacles, including resistance from some central banks and the influence of Western-leaning political forces in member countries, continue to slow strategic initiatives.
